findings.title: Unsubscribe template path does not match topicUnsubscribe route name
findings.body: This template is stored at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which Ember resolves for a nested topic.unsubscribe route. However app-route-map.js.es6 registers the route as top-level topicUnsubscribe, so Ember will look for templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs. As a result the unsubscribe route will render without its intended template (empty or missing template), so the new unsubscribe page is broken.

findings.title: unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser row exists
findings.body: TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) may return nil for users who received a notification (for example a mention, reply, or quote) without ever having a topic_users row. The next lines dereference tu.notification_level, causing NoMethodError. Use TopicUser.change(...) or find_or_initialize_by and handle the missing record, otherwise the unsubscribe page 500s for valid users.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url for all add_unsubscribe_link emails
findings.body: The shared unsubscribe_link text now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}. Email::MessageBuilder calls I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) for every message that sets add_unsubscribe_link: true, but only UserNotifications#send_notification_email has been updated in this diff to pass unsubscribe_url. Any other email using add_unsubscribe_link will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument or render a broken link. Either provide a default for unsubscribe_url, make the topic-specific sentence conditional, or update every caller.

findings.title: Unsubscribe is a state-changing GET without CSRF or unique token
findings.body: The new /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe routes are GET and directly change the user's notification_level. GET requests are not CSRF-protected and are treated as safe by clients, so a logged-in user can be unsubscribed by an embedded image, link prefetch, or email scanner following the URL. State changes should be POST/PUT with CSRF protection, or the link should include an unguessable per-user token.

findings.title: Unsubscribe renders stale serialized topic notification state
findings.body: @topic_view is constructed at line 99 before tu.notification_level is changed. perform_show_response then serializes that original @topic_view, so the preloaded JSON/HTML response contains the old notification level. The client's topic-notifications-button can show the pre-unsubscribe state, and another GET may be required to see the change. Rebuild @topic_view or update its topic-user data after saving.

findings.title: Direct tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
findings.body: Changing notification_level directly and calling save! does not set notifications_reason_id or notifications_changed_at, and does not publish the /topic/:id MessageBus update that TopicUser.change performs. Other live clients won't see the state change, and notification-change history/reasoning can become inconsistent. Use TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...) instead.
